answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rely on costly identity that is slow to build. Each agent gets a stake bonded to its key, and reputation accrues only after peers verify its work over many rounds. A glacier moves slowly but carries enormous weight, and similarly a new identity cannot gain trust quickly. Attackers spinning up thousands of fake agents hit a timber-like wall of accumulated history, while a canyon of rate limits and staggered challenges keeps any single operator from flooding the network.
